must_remember: Thermal neutrons have an energy of approximately $0.025\text{ eV}$ and are highly effective in causing fission of $\text{U-235}$.
The binding energy per nucleon increases from about $7.6\text{ MeV}$ for uranium to about $8.5\text{ MeV}$ for medium-mass fission fragments, releasing roughly $200\text{ MeV}$ per fission event.
The multiplication factor $k$ determines the state of a nuclear chain reactor: $k = 1$ (critical), $k < 1$ (subcritical), and $k > 1$ (supercritical).
Nuclear reactors utilize moderators like graphite, heavy water ($\text{D}_2\text{O}$), or ordinary water ($\text{H}_2\text{O}$) to slow down fast neutrons.
Control rods made of cadmium, boron, or hafnium have high neutron absorption cross-sections and are used to regulate or halt the chain reaction.

glossary.meaning: A neutron in thermal equilibrium with its surroundings, having an average kinetic energy of about $0.025\text{ eV}$.
The ratio of the number of neutrons in any generation to the number in the immediately preceding generation.
The point during nuclear fission when the elongated compound nucleus splits into two primary fission fragments.
A substance used in a nuclear reactor to slow down fast neutrons to thermal energies via elastic collisions without capturing them.
The difference between the total rest mass of the separate nucleons and the actual mass of the nucleus.
